title: Kagi import reads conversation.messages; real exports keep messages at the top level
description:
## Bug

Importing a real Kagi Assistant export produces an empty Graph with no error. Observed 2026-09-02 with the export "Telescope Buying Guide for Beginners" (6 messages, 12 references on the first answer): the imported project saved as `telescopes.thoughttree` has `version: 4`, 0 nodes, 0 edges.

Real export shape (top-level keys): `conversation`, `exported_at`, `messages`, `version`. `conversation` holds only `created_at`, `is_saved`, `is_shared`, `model_name`, `title`. `messages[]` is a **top-level** array, exactly as thoughttree-4hq's "Source format" section lists it.

Both implementations read `conversation.messages` instead:

- `packages/graph-model/src/kagi.ts:131` (`parseKagiExport`)
- `src-tauri/src/backend/commands/imports.rs` (`graph_from_kagi`, `conversation.get("messages")`)

and the sanitized fixture `test/fixtures/kagi-export-v1.json` was written with `conversation.messages`, so every test passed against the wrong shape.

## Fix

1. Read `messages` from the top level of the export. Keep `conversation.messages` as a fallback only if it costs nothing; the canonical shape is top-level.
2. Correct `test/fixtures/kagi-export-v1.json` to the real shape (top-level `messages`, `conversation` without `messages`). Keep everything else in the fixture unchanged.
3. An export whose Turn list is empty after pairing must fail with a typed, user-readable error (for example `Kagi export contains no messages`) in both the TypeScript parser and the Tauri command, and the frontend must not replace the current project. Nothing is created on error (thoughttree-4hq.3 contract).
4. Add a regression test in both seams that a fixture with top-level `messages` yields 2 Turns / 4 nodes, and that a version-1 export with an empty or missing `messages` array is rejected.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Importing the sanitized fixture end to end yields 4 nodes and 3 edges.
- [ ] A version-1 export with no messages is rejected with a user-readable error and the current project is untouched.
- [ ] `bun run test:run`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `./scripts/check-core-no-tauri.sh` pass.

title: Restore vault-boundary validation for Tauri project commands
description:
## Parent

- Mobile-push safety hardening

## What to build

Restore the configured-vault boundary for desktop Project load and save commands. A caller must not be able to use the Tauri IPC surface to read or overwrite arbitrary absolute paths outside the configured notes directory.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Load and save reject paths outside the configured notes directory.
- [ ] Relative traversal, absolute paths, and symlink escapes are rejected.
- [ ] Valid Projects inside the configured vault continue to load and save.
- [ ] Command-level tests cover both rejection and valid-path behavior.

## Blocked by

- None — can start immediately.

title: Close guarded-write compare-and-swap race
description:
## Parent

- Mobile-push safety hardening

## What to build

Ensure a guarded Project write validates the expected revision as part of the replacement operation, so a concurrent writer cannot update the file after the check and then be overwritten by the pending rename.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A forced interleaving test reproduces a concurrent update between revision validation and replacement.
- [ ] The guarded write rejects the stale replacement or otherwise preserves the concurrent writer's content.
- [ ] Successful guarded writes remain atomic and return the new revision.
- [ ] Existing stale-save behavior remains unchanged for callers.

## Blocked by

- None — can start immediately.

title: Mobile-push safety hardening
description:
## What to build

Make the shared project-storage guarantees safe for both the desktop shell and the future server. A concurrent writer must never be overwritten after a stale revision check, and desktop project commands must remain confined to the configured vault.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A concurrent-write test proves that a newer project revision cannot be overwritten after the guarded check.
- [ ] A stale write returns the current revision and leaves the newer file content intact.
- [ ] Tauri project load and save reject absolute paths outside the configured notes directory.
- [ ] Traversal and symlink escape cases remain rejected.
- [ ] Rust tests cover both the compare-and-swap race and vault-boundary enforcement.

## Blocked by

- None — can start immediately.

title: Consolidate Kagi import: one parser and transform, not Rust and TypeScript copies
description:
## Observation (orchestrator, not a review finding)

thoughttree-4hq.2 landed the Kagi export parser in TypeScript (`packages/graph-model/src/kagi.ts`) and thoughttree-1y9 landed the Provider-neutral conversation-to-Graph transform there too (`packages/graph-model/src/import.ts`). thoughttree-4hq.3 then implemented the Tauri command `import_kagi_export` with its own Rust parse + graph construction (`src-tauri/src/backend/commands/imports.rs`, `graph_from_kagi`), because the issue text said the backend runs the parser and the transformation.

Result: two independent implementations of version checking, message pairing, citation detection (`【n】`), reference field selection, deterministic ids, and layout. They will drift, and the Rust path bypasses the tested TypeScript seam and its follow-ups (thoughttree-efn, thoughttree-zl6, thoughttree-6ua).

## Decide and consolidate

Pick one:

1. Backend stays thin: the Tauri command only validates the path, enforces the byte cap on the opened handle, reads the file, and returns the raw export text (or a size-checked, version-checked string). The frontend runs `parseKagiExport` + `conversationToGraph`. Delete `graph_from_kagi`.
2. Backend owns import: move the parser and transform into the Rust core crate (keeping `./scripts/check-core-no-tauri.sh` green), delete the TypeScript parser/transform, and keep the transport contract as the Graph DTO.

Option 1 matches the shared-seam intent of the epics (Codex import thoughttree-836 also depends on the TypeScript transform). Either way the end-to-end test in `imports.rs` and the TypeScript fixture tests must exercise the same fixture and produce the same node ids.

title: Kagi import: enforce the byte cap on the opened file handle, not a separate metadata lookup
description:
## Deferred review finding from Issue Run thoughttree-4hq.3

### Finding `agent-755ed70c6f90ecac` (medium, src-tauri/src/backend/commands/imports.rs:199)

The size check and read operate on separate path lookups, and `fs::read` consumes the entire file before the second cap check. If the selected path is replaced or grows after `metadata`, the command can read a different or arbitrarily larger file into memory, bypassing the intended read-time cap. Open the file once, check metadata on that handle, and read through `take(KAGI_EXPORT_MAX_BYTES + 1)` before parsing.

**Evidence:** `git show 0f3f8f814dac0f523d39e5a16d834b4217c4668e:src-tauri/src/backend/commands/imports.rs | nl -ba | sed -n '190,207p'` shows `fs::metadata(path)` followed by a separate unbounded `fs::read(path)`, with the second limit check occurring only after allocation and reading complete.

**Failure scenario:** Select a small export and replace or enlarge it between the metadata check and `fs::read` -> the backend reads the replacement or oversized contents in full before rejecting them, defeating the size cap and potentially causing excessive memory use.

title: importGraph must reset project model and effort preferences for the imported project
description:
## Deferred review finding from Issue Run thoughttree-4hq.3

### Finding `agent-beb5572d61ac0284` (medium, src/store/useGraphStore.ts:752)

`importGraph` does not reset `projectModelPreferences` or `projectEffortPreferences`. Zustand's partial `set` therefore carries preferences from the previously open project into the imported project, and `saveProject` serializes those stale preferences. Reset both fields to `null` when installing the imported graph and add a store test covering import over a project with custom preferences.

**Evidence:** `sed -n '267,280p;650,765p' src/store/useGraphStore.ts` shows `serializeProjectFile` writes both preference fields, while the `importGraph` state update omits them; `rg -n "importGraph" src/store/useGraphStore.test.ts` finds no regression test.

**Failure scenario:** Open a project with project-specific model or effort preferences, import a Kagi export, then save it -> the newly created project file incorrectly contains preferences inherited from the prior project.

title: conversationToGraph must surface an incomplete trailing Turn in the Graph
description:
## Deferred review finding from Issue Run thoughttree-4hq.2 (review retry)

### Finding `agent-7cc060199a7e615f` (medium, packages/graph-model/src/import.ts:6)

The new `incomplete` flag is not consumed by `conversationToGraph`, so converting parser output into the application's graph discards the distinction between an unanswered trailing user message and a completed assistant message with empty content. Propagate the state into the graph's canonical representation—such as an explicit assistant-node flag or partial/incomplete provenance—and add an integration test from `parseKagiExport` through `conversationToGraph`.

**Evidence:** The focused runtime probe parsed a trailing user message and then called `conversationToGraph`. Observed parsed turn: `{"userMessage":"unanswered","assistantAnswer":"","incomplete":true}`; observed assistant node: `{"id":"import:Kagi%20conversation:turn:0:assistant","role":"assistant","content":"","timestamp":1}`, with no incomplete state or provenance.

**Failure scenario:** A version-1 export ends with an unanswered user message -> the parser correctly marks the DTO turn incomplete -> `conversationToGraph` drops that flag -> persisted and displayed graph data treats the generated empty assistant node as indistinguishable from a completed empty answer.

title: Harden Kagi parser input handling: cap bytes before encoding, reject malformed UTF-8
description:
## Deferred review findings from Issue Run thoughttree-4hq.2 (review retry)

Both concern untrusted-input handling at the Kagi parser entry (`parseKagiExport`): enforce the byte cap before materializing the full encoded input, and decode with `TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true })` so malformed bytes produce the typed error instead of silent U+FFFD replacement.

### Finding `agent-758d37d8e0bf020f` (medium, packages/graph-model/src/kagi.ts:104)

The string path computes its byte length by fully UTF-8-encoding the input before checking `maxBytes`, so an arbitrarily oversized untrusted string can cause a correspondingly large allocation or OOM instead of the typed `input_too_large` rejection the cap is intended to provide. Reject first when `input.length > maxBytes`—UTF-8 byte length cannot be smaller than the JavaScript code-unit length—then encode only inputs that pass that cheap bound and perform the exact byte check.

**Evidence:** Focused probe patched `TextEncoder.encode` and called `parseKagiExport` with 16,777,217 characters. Observed: `encode_called_with=16777217` followed by the probe's generic `Error: encoder sentinel`, proving encoding occurs before the cap can reject the input.

**Failure scenario:** A caller passes a very large string export -> `TextEncoder` allocates for the entire attacker-controlled string before line 115 checks the limit -> the process can suffer memory pressure or terminate instead of returning `KagiExportError` with `input_too_large`.

### Finding `agent-8e8d304ec8fd96f6` (medium, packages/graph-model/src/kagi.ts:107)

`TextDecoder` uses its default lossy mode, so malformed UTF-8 bytes inside otherwise valid JSON are silently replaced with U+FFFD and accepted. This corrupts assistant content instead of preserving it or rejecting invalid input. Decode with `new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true })`, translate decoding failures to the typed `invalid_json` error, and add a malformed-byte test.

**Evidence:** The focused runtime probe supplied a `Uint8Array` containing byte `0x80` inside the assistant JSON string. `parseKagiExport` succeeded and returned `malformedUtf8Result:"�"` rather than throwing `KagiExportError`.

**Failure scenario:** A Kagi export contains malformed UTF-8 in an assistant answer -> decoding silently substitutes U+FFFD -> the returned DTO contains altered answer text despite the content-preservation contract.

title: Kagi parser must accept only http/https reference URLs
description:
## Deferred review finding from Issue Run thoughttree-4hq.2

Related: thoughttree-3c5 (export autolink scheme check), thoughttree-74u (load/save normalization). This one is the parser seam: Kagi references are web-only, so the parser should keep only http/https URLs as clickable references and demote anything else to a non-clickable display value.

### Finding `agent-b518c35328a1286c` (medium, packages/graph-model/src/kagi.ts:56)

Reference normalization accepts every string-valued `url`, including `file:` and other non-web schemes, despite the contract that Kagi references are web-only. This allows an untrusted export to place an external absolute path into the provider-neutral DTO; `conversationToGraph` and project serialization preserve it, and the existing Markdown formatter emits it as an autolink. Validate URLs without dereferencing them and retain only `http:`/`https:` references (or safely omit invalid/non-web references), with an adversarial test.

**Evidence:** A temporary Vitest probe passed `url: "file:///Users/alice/private.txt"`; `parseKagiExport` returned `{"type":"url","url":"file:///Users/alice/private.txt","relations":["cited"],"title":"Local evidence","index":1}`. Static tracing shows `packages/graph-model/src/import.ts:72` copies the provenance into the graph, `packages/graph-model/src/serialize.ts:29` persists it, and `src/store/useGraphStore.ts:173` formats it as `<file:///Users/alice/private.txt>`.

**Failure scenario:** Importing a modified Kagi export containing a `file:///Users/alice/private.txt` reference causes that external absolute path to be stored in the graph/project and emitted in a later Markdown export as an autolink instead of being rejected as non-web data.

title: Markdown export must only autolink http/https provenance URLs
description:
## Deferred review finding from Issue Run thoughttree-81u.2

Related: thoughttree-74u (runtime normalization of provenance on load/save). This issue covers the export seam specifically: only http and https URL references may be autolinked in Markdown export; other schemes must be emitted as plain text.

### Finding `agent-db67834a2ef96863` (medium, src/store/useGraphStore.ts:173)

Every URL reference is wrapped in Markdown autolink syntax without checking its scheme. Because v4 project data is loaded without runtime validation, a `file://` URL is exported verbatim and can expose an external absolute path, contrary to the requirement that exports not emit such paths and the project rule that only HTTP(S) URLs are clickable. Only autolink validated HTTP(S) URLs; reject or safely redact `file:` URLs and render other schemes as escaped, non-clickable text. Add coverage for non-HTTP and `file://` references.

**Evidence:** A temporary Vitest probe against commit cf55feb created an assistant reference with `url: "file:///Users/alice/private.txt"`. `TAURI_DEV_HOST=127.0.0.1 npm run test:run -- src/store/review-url-export.test.ts` exited 0 and printed `1. **URL:** Local evidence — <file:///Users/alice/private.txt> — Relations: consulted`. The responsible formatter is `return `${index}. **URL:** ${title}<${reference.url}> — Relations: ${relations}`;` at line 173.

**Failure scenario:** Opening or importing a v4 project containing a non-HTTP URL reference such as `file:///Users/alice/private.txt`, then exporting that assistant lineage, produces Markdown containing the external absolute path as an autolink instead of a safe non-clickable or redacted reference.

title: Normalize Turn provenance on load/save so raw payloads and absolute paths are never persisted
description:
## Deferred review findings from Issue Run thoughttree-81u.1

Both findings describe the same defect: `toJSON` persists GraphNode objects wholesale and `fromJSON` performs no runtime normalization, so provenance loaded from a v4 Project file or supplied by a provider can carry raw tool input/output, command text, unknown raw payloads, or absolute external paths into the saved Project file. This violates the thoughttree-81u persistence constraint.

## Fix

Rebuild provenance from an explicit field allowlist at the load or save boundary, validate that vault paths are relative, and add an adversarial round-trip test containing every forbidden field.

### Finding `agent-495a56b9e204e577` (medium, packages/graph-model/src/serialize.ts:29)

`toJSON` serializes each `GraphNode` wholesale, while `fromJSON` accepts parsed node objects without runtime normalization. TypeScript interfaces therefore do not enforce the requirement that persisted provenance exclude raw tool input/output, command text, unknown payloads, or external absolute paths. Rebuild provenance from an explicit field allowlist at the load or save boundary, validate that vault paths are relative, and add an adversarial round-trip test containing every forbidden field.

**Evidence:** Running a `bun -e` round-trip probe against the target snapshot produced: {"completeness":"partial","references":[{"type":"file","scope":"vault","path":"/Users/alice/secret.txt","displayName":"secret.txt","relations":["read"],"rawPayload":{"token":"secret"}}],"activity":[{"type":"tool","kind":"execute","title":"Run command","status":"completed","rawInput":"cat /Users/alice/secret.txt","rawOutput":"secret contents","command":"cat /Users/alice/secret.txt"},{"type":"unknown","providerType":"x","label":"x","payload":{"token":"secret"}}]}.

**Failure scenario:** A v4 project is loaded, or a provider supplies a structurally compatible node, containing raw tool fields or an absolute path; `fromJSON` retains those properties and `toJSON` writes them back, causing sensitive command data, tool output, unknown payloads, or host paths to be observably persisted in the saved Project file.

### Finding `agent-709a3be299753812` (medium, packages/graph-model/src/serialize.ts:29)

`toJSON` persists node objects wholesale and `fromJSON` performs no runtime normalization. Parsed or provider-supplied data can therefore persist provenance on user nodes, arbitrary raw input/output/payload fields, absolute Vault paths, and command text—including command text hidden in the allowed `title` field. This can leak sensitive local data into saved Project files. Serialize provenance through an explicit role-aware allowlist, reject or remove provenance from non-assistant nodes, require relative Vault paths, and ensure tool titles are sanitized summaries rather than raw commands. Add an adversarial load/save test covering extra fields and forbidden content inside allowed fields.

**Evidence:** `bun /tmp/thoughttree-review-f2a5ab9/provenance-probe.ts` exited 0 and serialized an assistant provenance object containing `/Users/alice/secret.txt`, `rawPayload`, `commandText`, `rawInput`, `rawOutput`, an unknown `payload`, and the raw command in `title`; it also serialized provenance on a user node unchanged.

**Failure scenario:** Trigger: a provider adapter or imported v4 Project supplies raw tool fields, a command as the tool title, an absolute Vault path, or provenance on a user node. Because serialization copies nodes verbatim, saving the Project writes those forbidden values to disk, producing an observably unsafe v4 file rather than sanitized assistant-only provenance.

title: File-based import transport seam for Kagi exports
description:
## Outcome

The user picks a Kagi export file from the desktop app and gets a new Graph. The transport exposes a single import operation without leaking file-system details into frontend state.

## Behavior

- Frontend: an Import entry (command palette and/or menu) opens a native file picker filtered to `.json`.
- Backend Tauri command receives the picked path, checks size cap, reads the file, runs the Kagi parser, runs the Provider-neutral transformation, and returns the Graph to the frontend.
- The frontend opens the returned Graph as an unsaved Project titled from `conversation.title`.
- Errors (unsupported version, too large, invalid JSON) surface as a user-readable message. Nothing is created on error.

## Security

- The picked path is used once and never persisted in the Project file or in stores.
- Only the file the user selected is read. No directory enumeration.
- The transport type for the import result is the Graph DTO, not raw JSON.

## Success Criteria

[ ] TauriTransport has an import method with a mocked test.
[ ] Importing the sanitized fixture end to end yields a Graph with the expected node count.
[ ] Project file written after import contains no absolute path to the source export.
[ ] Error cases show a message and leave the current Project untouched.

title: Parse Kagi export v1 into the Provider-neutral conversation DTO
description:
## Outcome

A parser turns Kagi export JSON into the Provider-neutral conversation DTO. It is pure, tolerant of unknown fields, and strict on the export version.

## Behavior

- Accept `version: 1`. Reject other versions with a typed error naming the version found.
- Pair messages into Turns: each user message followed by its assistant message. A trailing user message without an answer becomes a Turn with an empty answer flagged as incomplete, not an error.
- Assistant `content` copied byte-for-byte into the Turn answer. `【n】` markers are not rewritten.
- `references[]` mapped into thoughttree-81u provenance references. A reference is cited when its `index` appears as a `【n】` marker in the same message's `content`, consulted otherwise. Record `is_search_result` separately as the source kind (search hit vs fetched page). Persist `url`, `title`, `domain`, `index`, `percentage`, `is_search_result`. Drop `snippet`, `favicon`, `passages`.
- Per-message `model_name` recorded on the Turn.
- Unknown fields ignored. Missing optional fields default cleanly.
- Enforce an input size cap before parsing (proposal: 16 MB).

## Security

- No network access. Never dereference `url` or `favicon`.
- Treat all strings as data. No path handling; Kagi references are web-only.

## Success Criteria

[ ] Sanitized fixture parses into the expected DTO snapshot.
[ ] `version: 99` fixture is rejected with the typed error.
[ ] Snippets, favicons, and passages are absent from the DTO.
[ ] A reference with `is_search_result: true` whose index is cited inline is marked cited; an uncited reference with `is_search_result: false` is marked consulted.
[ ] Property test or table test covers missing `references`, empty `messages`, and role sequences that do not alternate.
[ ] Parser has no Tauri dependency and passes `./scripts/check-core-no-tauri.sh` if placed in core.

title: Sanitized Kagi export fixture
description:
## Outcome

A small, committed Kagi export fixture that exercises every shape the parser must handle, without any personal content.

## Contents

- `version: 1`, `exported_at`, `conversation` with a neutral title and `model_name`.
- Two message pairs (user, assistant, user, assistant).
- First assistant message: three references. Index 1 `is_search_result: false`, cited via `【1】`. Index 2 `is_search_result: true`, cited via `【2】`. Index 3 `is_search_result: true`, not cited. Content also contains `【9】` with no matching reference.
- Second assistant message: no `references` key at all.
- One unknown top-level field and one unknown message field, to prove tolerance.
- `passages: null` on one reference, a short populated `passages` array on another.
- Assistant metadata fields (`tokens`, `cost_usd`, `duration_ms`, `model_version`) present with harmless values.

Also add a second tiny fixture with `version: 99` for the unsupported-version rejection test.

## Success Criteria

[ ] Fixture is under 5 KB and contains no real URLs beyond example.com domains.
[ ] Fixture exercises cited search hit, cited fetched page, consulted-only, dangling marker, missing `references`, unknown fields, null and populated passages.
[ ] Fixture is used by parser tests and by the end-to-end import test.

title: Provider-neutral conversation-to-Graph transformation with deterministic ids
description:
## Outcome

A pure, Provider-neutral transformation turns an imported conversation DTO into a Graph: GraphNodes, GraphEdges, Layout, and Turn provenance, with deterministic ids. Both historical import epics (Codex thoughttree-836, Kagi Assistant) depend on this seam so that Provider parsing and Graph construction stay independently testable.

## Scope

- Define a Provider-neutral conversation DTO: ordered Turns, each with a user message, exact assistant final answer (Markdown, byte-for-byte), optional model name, optional timestamps, and optional Turn provenance in the thoughttree-81u model (references, activity, unknown items).
- Pure function DTO -> Graph. No IO, no Tauri, no Provider knowledge.
- Deterministic ids derived from a stable import key (source id or content hash) plus Turn index, so that re-import of the same source produces the same ids.
- Optional Turn-range selection (start/end index) applied before transformation.
- Linear chain: each assistant GraphNode is a child of its user GraphNode, each user GraphNode a child of the previous assistant GraphNode.
- Unknown provenance items are retained as inspectable unknown entries, never dropped and never fatal.
- Result is a new Graph only. Merge into an existing Graph and update-by-external-id are out of scope; record the decision.

## Non-goals

- Reading any Provider format. Adapters live in their own epics.
- UI. No import dialog here.

## Security and privacy

- The transformation must not persist raw tool input or output; it consumes the already-normalized provenance model.
- Paths in provenance are assumed already Vault-relative or redacted by the adapter; the transform must not widen them.

## Success Criteria

[ ] Exact assistant Markdown survives transformation unchanged.
[ ] Same DTO in, same Graph out: ids, edges, and layout are deterministic across runs.
[ ] Turn-range selection excludes Turns outside the range and renumbers nothing that would change ids of included Turns.
[ ] Unknown provenance items appear in the output provenance as unknown entries.
[ ] Unit tests use only in-memory DTO fixtures; no Provider fixture is required.
[ ] `./scripts/check-core-no-tauri.sh` still passes if the transform lands in core.

## Depends on

- thoughttree-81u: Turn provenance model in Project-file v4.

title: Import Kagi Assistant conversation exports with exact answers and cited sources
description:
## Outcome

A user can import a Kagi Assistant conversation export (JSON file) into a new ThoughtTree Graph. Exact assistant Markdown is preserved, and each assistant GraphNode carries the cited and consulted web sources that Kagi attached to that message.

This epic owns the Kagi-facing import seam: file selection, schema validation, normalization of the export into the Provider-neutral conversation DTO, and citation-to-reference mapping. Graph construction is shared with the Codex import epic (thoughttree-836) through the Provider-neutral transformation feature.

## Source format (observed, export `version: 1`)

Kagi exports one conversation per file from the web UI, as JSON or Markdown. JSON is the import source; see decision 5. Observed shape from two real exports (6 and 2 messages; `Telescope Buying Guide for Beginners`, `Spaghettifizierung: Empfindungen bei einem Schwarzen Loch`):

- `version`: 1
- `exported_at`: ISO timestamp
- `conversation`: `{ title, model_name, is_saved, is_shared, created_at }`
- `messages[]`: `{ role: "user" | "assistant", content, created_at }`
- assistant messages additionally carry `model_name`, `model_version`, `tokens`, `tokens_per_second`, `cost_usd`, `duration_ms`, `references[]`
- `references[]`: `{ index, url, source, title, domain, favicon, snippet, percentage, is_search_result, ref_id, passages }`
- assistant `content` cites references inline with markers of the form `【n】` where `n` matches `references[].index`
- `passages` is null in one sample and populated in the other; treat as optional and do not persist
- `conversation.model_name` may be a Kagi alias (`ki_quick`) rather than a model id; per-message `model_name` is the reliable one

Differences from the Codex import:

- Input is a user-selected file, not a Provider process or session id.
- No tool activity, no commentary phases, no Turn ranges needed by default.
- Provenance is already structured per message. Cited vs consulted (thoughttree-81u user story 3) is derived from the inline `【n】` markers: a reference is cited when its `index` appears in the answer, consulted otherwise. `is_search_result` is orthogonal: `true` = web-search hit, `false` = page Kagi fetched and read in full (its `snippet` is then a page summary). Both kinds can be cited; in the samples, fetched pages are cited most.
- Model name is per message, not per conversation, and belongs in GraphNode provenance rather than in the Provider id.

## Decisions to record during refinement

1. Which reference fields persist. Proposal: `url`, `title`, `domain`, `index`, `is_search_result`, `percentage`. Drop `snippet`, `favicon`, `passages` by default; snippets are long third-party excerpts and favicon URLs are Kagi proxy links.
2. Whether to persist token, cost, and duration metadata. Proposal: no for the first release.
3. Which Provider id the imported Graph uses, given no `kagi` Provider exists. Proposal: a read-only import Provider marker rather than a live Provider.
4. Whether the `【n】` markers stay in the Markdown untouched. Proposal: yes, exact content is the contract; the SidePanel provenance section resolves them.
5. JSON vs Markdown export as import source. Decided: JSON. The Markdown export is lossy: it rewrites `【n】` to `[^n]` footnotes and appends a References block, drops per-message model, timestamps, `domain`, `is_search_result`, `snippet`, and metadata, and delimits turns with `**You**` / `**Assistant**` / `---` lines that can collide with answer content. JSON carries a `version` field and needs no heuristic parsing. Markdown export stays out of scope; ThoughtTree produces its own Markdown via thoughttree-81u.2.

## Security and privacy constraints

- The export is untrusted JSON chosen by the user. Enforce a size cap, reject unknown `version` values with a clear error, and tolerate unknown fields.
- Never store the absolute path of the selected file in the Project file.
- Do not fetch favicons, sources, or any URL during import.
- Do not commit the real export. Build a small sanitized fixture with a short conversation, one cited reference, one consulted-only reference, one inline citation marker, and one unknown field.

## Success Criteria

[ ] Importing the sanitized fixture produces one user and one assistant GraphNode per message pair, linked linearly.
[ ] Exact assistant Markdown, including `【n】` markers, survives byte-for-byte.
[ ] Each cited reference appears under the correct assistant GraphNode with cited vs consulted distinguished.
[ ] Unknown top-level or message fields do not fail import.
[ ] An export with an unsupported `version` fails with an actionable error and creates nothing.
[ ] The selected file path is not persisted.
[ ] Manual validation against the real export `Telescope Buying Guide for Beginners` succeeds without committing it.

## Depends on

- thoughttree-81u: Turn provenance model.
- Provider-neutral conversation-to-Graph transformation feature.

title: Mobile server and PWA
description:
## What to build

Deliver the browser-served ThoughtTree path in progressively usable slices: browse and edit Projects through HTTP, stream server-owned Turns with replay after disconnect, and resume parked permission requests when a client reattaches.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A browser or installed PWA can list, open, edit, and guarded-save Projects through the server.
- [ ] A prompt streams through a server-owned Turn and remains recoverable if the client disconnects.
- [ ] Reattachment replays active or completed Turns and applies them through the existing GraphModel path.
- [ ] A permission request can remain parked while no client is attached and is surfaced first on reattach.
- [ ] The desktop transport and permission flow remain unchanged.

## Blocked by

- Mobile-push safety hardening
- Mobile-usage validation evidence

title: Remote storage and NAS deployment
description:
## What to build

Make the mobile server usable against the real synced vault and deploy it to the NAS over the private tailnet. Validate the mobile workflow first, then add WebDAV compare-and-swap storage and the production deployment/runbook.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Mobile-usage validation evidence is recorded and the stopgap workflow is accepted.
- [ ] The WebDAV vault reads, lists, and guarded-writes Projects with reliable ETag compare-and-swap semantics.
- [ ] WebDAV credentials are sourced safely and never appear in logs or errors.
- [ ] The NAS stack serves the PWA over Tailscale with guarded saves, live Turns, permission prompts, and detached-turn recovery.
- [ ] Deployment, rollback, secret rotation, and vault read-only mount behavior are documented.

## Blocked by

- Mobile-push safety hardening

title: Inspect Turn provenance safely in the SidePanel
description:
## Parent

thoughttree-81u: Turn provenance: persist and render sources, files, commentary, and tool activity

## What to build

A user inspecting an assistant GraphNode can expand one collapsed Provenance disclosure below the exact answer. The disclosure summarizes source, file, and activity counts, then presents safe canonical references before the chronological Turn activity. Incomplete evidence is visibly distinguished from an empty Turn.

Use the shared sanitized version-4 fixture at the SidePanel behavior seam. Provenance remains absent from Graph cards, and rendering untrusted historical data must not execute tool content, open external paths, or broaden ThoughtTree permissions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Assistant GraphNodes with provenance show one collapsed Provenance disclosure below the exact answer; GraphNodes without provenance retain the existing presentation.
- [ ] The disclosure label reports source, file, and activity counts derived from canonical persisted provenance.
- [ ] Expanded content presents references before Turn activity and preserves reference first-appearance order and authoritative activity order.
- [ ] URL and file relations are visible; only HTTP and HTTPS URLs are clickable, Vault files use their relative paths, and external files remain non-clickable display names.
- [ ] Partial and unknown Provenance completeness display a warning that missing evidence is possible.
- [ ] Assistant commentary and Tool-activity details start collapsed, while Tool kind and state remain understandable without raw input or output.
- [ ] Tool titles are rendered as untrusted plain text, limited to 200 characters, and visibly identified when truncated.
- [ ] Unknown activity is inspectable through its safe type name and display label without retaining or rendering its raw payload.
- [ ] Graph cards remain unchanged.
- [ ] SidePanel behavior is covered with the shared sanitized version-4 fixture, and the complete repository test suite and production build pass.

## Blocked by

- thoughttree-81u.1: Persist Turn provenance in Project-file v4.

title: Persist Turn provenance in Project-file v4
description:
## Parent

thoughttree-81u: Turn provenance: persist and render sources, files, commentary, and tool activity

## What to build

A Project file can preserve provider-neutral Turn provenance on an assistant GraphNode without rewriting the exact answer or changing the Conversation path. Project-file version 4 becomes the current format, while every legacy format currently supported by ThoughtTree continues to load without Graph-data loss.

Use one sanitized version-4 fixture across the Graph model, Project, and Conversation behavior seams. The fixture must represent canonical URL and file references, additive relations, ordered Assistant commentary, one logical Tool activity, Unknown activity, incomplete provenance, and a truncated tool title without retaining raw payloads, command text, or external absolute paths.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Provider-neutral discriminated types represent Provenance completeness, URL and file Turn references, Assistant commentary, Tool activity, and Unknown activity only on assistant GraphNodes.
- [ ] Turn-reference order and Turn-activity array order survive Graph serialization unchanged, including additive relations and optional timestamps.
- [ ] A sanitized version-4 Project fixture loads through the Graph store and saves again with the exact assistant content and observable provenance unchanged.
- [ ] Every currently supported legacy Project format loads with its existing Graph data intact and without inventing Turn provenance.
- [ ] Unsupported future Project-file versions are rejected instead of being treated as legacy data.
- [ ] Building a Conversation path from a GraphNode with provenance produces the same model context as the same GraphNode without provenance.
- [ ] Persisted provenance contains no raw tool input, raw tool output, command text, unknown raw payload, or external absolute path.
- [ ] Graph-model tests, Project behavior tests, Conversation-path tests, the complete repository test suite, and the production build pass.

## Blocked by

title: Capture live ACP tool activity as GraphNode provenance
description:
## Outcome

Tool-call activity received during a live ACP Turn is captured, updated, persisted, and shown as provenance on the assistant GraphNode that receives the response.

This epic owns the event path from ACP notifications through the backend transport into the same provider-neutral provenance model used by historical import.

> Refinement status: this is seeded context from the Codex-session provenance handoff, not a settled specification. Event ownership, accumulation details, raw-data policy, and the first demo slice remain open.

## Established implementation gap

ThoughtTree already receives live ACP tool-call start and update notifications. The streaming ACP client currently logs them and drops them:

- They do not cross the backend session-event seam.
- They do not reach a frontend transport event.
- They are not associated with or persisted on the streaming assistant GraphNode.
- The existing tool-call backlog idea is UI-only and does not address this data path.

The ACP data available at the investigated version already includes a tool-call id, title, kind, status, content, locations, raw input, and raw output. ThoughtTree should normalize the useful and safe subset rather than expose Provider/ACP payloads directly to the frontend.

## Candidate event path

The likely vertical path is:

ACP client notification → backend SessionEventSink → Tauri/server event transport → focused per-Turn accumulator → assistant GraphNode provenance → Project-file persistence → SidePanel.

The same provider-neutral event model should be used for imported and live activity. Tool calls remain metadata on an assistant GraphNode, not standalone GraphNodes.

Incremental update merging should be hidden in a focused accumulator keyed by tool-call id. Avoid spreading patch logic across the ACP client, event sink, transport implementations, and Zustand store. Exact ownership remains a refinement decision.

## Required behavior and invariants

- A start plus any number of updates for one tool-call id collapse into one ordered final activity entry.
- Pending, in-progress, completed, and failed status changes behave deterministically.
- Tool order remains stable even when updates arrive later.
- Activity is associated with the correct Turn and streaming assistant GraphNode.
- Unknown/new tool kinds degrade to a safe generic representation.
- Provider-specific ACP shapes do not leak into the frontend domain model.
- Tool activity remains inspectable metadata and does not enter the Conversation path.
- Live capture does not broaden the current read-only ThoughtTree tool policy.

## Security and privacy constraints

- Raw input and output can contain secrets, personal data, file contents, or huge terminal logs.
- Do not persist full raw output by default.
- Decide explicit summary, redaction, truncation, and maximum-size rules before exposing raw details.
- Normalize file locations safely; Vault files should be Vault-relative where possible.
- Rendering must treat titles, summaries, locations, and Provider content as untrusted.
- Provenance handling must never execute tool input or replay historical activity.

## Refinement questions

1. Where should the tool-call accumulator live and when is it flushed into the GraphNode?
2. Which ACP fields become canonical activity fields, summaries, references, or discarded raw details?
3. How do events map to a Turn and GraphNode across desktop and future server deployment shapes?
4. Are commentary events captured through the same backend event path in this epic or separately?
5. What happens when an update arrives before a start, after completion, or with a reused id?
6. How should cancellation, transport loss, process failure, and incomplete tools be represented?
7. Should UI update incrementally during streaming or only persist finalized activity?
8. What privacy defaults and size limits apply to raw input/output and file locations?

## Candidate refinement sequence

- Add accumulator tests for start/update collapse, ordering, failure, unknown kind, and incomplete sequences.
- Extend the backend event seam with a minimal Provider-neutral tool activity event.
- Carry that event through each relevant BackendTransport implementation.
- Attach live activity to the streaming assistant GraphNode and persist it.
- Render it through the shared provenance SidePanel.
- Verify the final tool entry count and status against a real ACP Turn.

These are refinement inputs, not approved child tickets.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Live ACP tool-call start and update events reach the correct assistant GraphNode.
- [ ] Multiple updates collapse into one final activity entry per tool-call id with stable order and status.
- [ ] Out-of-order, incomplete, failed, and unknown activity shapes degrade safely.
- [ ] Captured activity survives Project-file save/load and appears in the shared provenance UI.
- [ ] Provider/ACP-specific payloads do not become frontend domain types.
- [ ] Activity does not enter Conversation-path prompts.
- [ ] Tool input is never executed and sensitive raw output is not persisted by default.
- [ ] Backend, transport, accumulation, persistence, and UI behavior have focused tests.
- [ ] A real ACP Turn demonstrates one final persisted entry per tool-call id.

## Blocked by

- thoughttree-81u: Turn provenance: persist and render sources, files, commentary, and tool activity.

title: Import historical Codex sessions with exact answers and provenance
description:
## Outcome

A user can import selected turns from a historical Codex session into a ThoughtTree Graph without rewriting the conversation. Exact final-answer Markdown and available turn provenance are attached to the correct assistant GraphNodes.

This epic owns the Codex-facing import seam, session and turn selection, deterministic mapping into a Graph, and safe normalization of Codex data.

> Refinement status: this is seeded context from the Codex-session provenance handoff, not a settled specification. The semantic fidelity target, import source, UI flow, and re-import behavior remain open.

## Validation case and established diagnosis

The motivating Codex session is `019fd7c4-3fca-77d3-9a4e-7c3b61135d71`. The requested conversation is its first five substantive user Turns; a sixth Turn asks Codex to construct the Graph and is intentionally self-referential.

For those first five Turns, the raw session contains:

- 23 tool invocations.
- Four distinct cited web URLs in final answers.
- Four distinct local Markdown-note references in final answers.

The manually generated Project file has 10 GraphNodes and nine GraphEdges but represents none of those tools or references. It also condenses the assistant answers. This was not a native import: Codex inspected another Graph and manually authored a legacy version-1 Project file. It used legacy Provider value `openai-codex`; the current Provider id is `codex`.

Do not commit the full rollout. It is roughly 723 KB and contains personal instructions, local paths, tool inputs/outputs, and private note context. Build a small sanitized fixture that preserves only the relevant event shapes.

## Source investigation already completed

The locally investigated Codex CLI app server supports initializing and reading a thread with Turns included. For this validation session it returned six Turns with structured semantic items:

- Six user messages.
- Eighteen assistant messages phased as commentary or final answer.
- Four web searches with query/result metadata.
- Two sub-agent activities.
- One file change.

This makes the Codex app server the preferred semantic boundary: it strips bootstrap developer/system messages and groups items into Turns.

However, persisted app-server history is lossy. It omitted some raw custom/function tool calls, including local note-reading shell activity. The rollout JSONL retained all 23 invocations.

## Import strategies to refine

1. Semantic MVP: import app-server items plus explicit Markdown references. Document that generic historical tool calls can be absent.
2. Enriched import: use the app server for Turns and final answers, then supplement tool records from a version-aware rollout reader by id/timestamp.
3. Raw-only import: parse rollout JSONL directly for maximum detail, accepting tight coupling to an internal and versioned format plus bootstrap filtering.

The handoff recommends strategy 1 unless exhaustive historical command activity is an explicit acceptance requirement. Whatever strategy wins, the provider-neutral import boundary should allow later enrichment without changing the Graph provenance model or UI.

## Candidate seam and behavior

A deep seam may resemble importing a Provider session by session id and optional Turn range into a Provider-neutral conversation DTO, followed by a pure transformation into a Graph. Exact API names and process placement are not decided.

Potential responsibilities:

- A Provider adapter invokes the Codex app server safely, or reads a known rollout format if refinement chooses enrichment.
- BackendTransport exposes session import without leaking app-server JSON-RPC into frontend code.
- A pure GraphModel transformation creates GraphNodes, GraphEdges, Layout, and provenance with deterministic ids.
- Turn-range selection can exclude the sixth self-referential Turn.
- Unknown Codex items normalize to an inspectable unknown event rather than failing or vanishing.
- Explicit Markdown citations and file links remain intact because final answers are not rewritten.

## Security and privacy constraints

- Validate session identifiers; never interpolate arbitrary values into shell commands.
- Prefer direct process arguments and stdio JSON-RPC to shell construction.
- Never execute imported tool input.
- Do not persist full raw tool output by default.
- Normalize Vault paths to Vault-relative form and avoid storing the OS username.
- Do not commit or rely on the private source rollout or temporary app-server responses.

## Refinement questions

1. Must the first release show every historical raw tool invocation, or are semantic web/file activities plus exact citations sufficient?
2. Should import default to all Turns or expose a Turn-range selector?
3. Is import new-Graph-only, merge into the current Graph, or update previously imported GraphNodes by external ids?
4. How should deterministic ids and duplicate detection behave across re-import?
5. Should model provenance be recovered from rollout turn context when the app server omits it?
6. Where does Provider-process normalization live relative to the transport and GraphModel?
7. What user-facing warning communicates incomplete historical tool activity?
8. Which references come from exact Markdown parsing versus normalized Provider events?

## Candidate refinement sequence

- Add a sanitized red import/round-trip fixture with exact final content, one citation, one file reference, commentary, a web search, a tool update, and an unknown item.
- Build the pure Provider-neutral conversation-to-Graph transformation with deterministic ids and Turn-range support.
- Add independent tests for Codex app-server normalization.
- Add the import transport/process seam.
- Validate manually against the private real session without committing it.
- Assess rollout enrichment only after the semantic path is usable.

These are refinement inputs, not approved child tickets.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Exact final-answer Markdown survives import byte-for-byte.
- [ ] Selecting the first five validation Turns produces 10 primary GraphNodes and nine linear GraphEdges.
- [ ] The four explicit URLs and four local note references are visible in the imported Project file.
- [ ] Available semantic web-search and file-change activity appears under the correct assistant GraphNode.
- [ ] A sanitized fixture covers commentary, activity updates, references, and an unknown Provider item.
- [ ] Unknown/new Codex item kinds do not crash import or disappear silently.
- [ ] Import is deterministic enough for the re-import behavior selected during refinement.
- [ ] Session ids and paths are handled without injection or unnecessary path disclosure.
- [ ] Provider normalization and Graph transformation are independently testable.
- [ ] The private rollout is not committed and raw output is not persisted accidentally.

title: Turn provenance: persist and render sources, files, commentary, and tool activity
description:
## Problem Statement

ThoughtTree preserves an assistant answer but loses the evidence and visible activity that produced it. Sources, files, commentary, and tool use disappear.

This loss makes historical imports incomplete. It also prevents live Turns from presenting useful provenance after the response is complete.

Exact Markdown can preserve explicit links. It cannot represent consulted resources, file activity, tool status, or Assistant commentary by itself.

## Solution

Add optional, provider-neutral Turn provenance to an assistant GraphNode. Keep the exact final answer in the GraphNode content.

Turn provenance stores canonical references and ordered Turn activity. It remains outside the Conversation path and does not create extra GraphNodes.

Show provenance in one collapsed SidePanel section below the answer. Keep Graph cards unchanged.

Store the new model in Project-file version 4. Migrate all legacy formats that the current application supports.

## User Stories

1. As a ThoughtTree user, I want the exact assistant answer preserved, so that provenance does not rewrite the conversation.
2. As a ThoughtTree user, I want to inspect cited sources, so that I can review evidence behind an answer.
3. As a ThoughtTree user, I want to distinguish cited and consulted URLs, so that I understand how each source contributed.
4. As a ThoughtTree user, I want to see referenced files, so that I understand which local material affected a Turn.
5. As a ThoughtTree user, I want file relations such as read or modified, so that a file name has useful context.
6. As a ThoughtTree user, I want visible Assistant commentary in order, so that I can review the progress reported during a Turn.
7. As a ThoughtTree user, I want one entry for each tool invocation, so that lifecycle updates do not clutter the activity list.
8. As a ThoughtTree user, I want tool status and kind, so that I can understand what happened without reading raw payloads.
9. As a ThoughtTree user, I want incomplete provenance identified, so that missing activity does not look like an empty Turn.
10. As a ThoughtTree user, I want unknown Provider activity retained safely, so that new event types do not disappear or break loading.
11. As a privacy-conscious user, I want raw tool input and output omitted, so that Project files do not collect terminal logs or secrets.
12. As a privacy-conscious user, I want external paths redacted, so that Project files do not expose usernames or machine-specific directories.
13. As a Vault user, I want Vault files shown with relative paths, so that references remain useful across synced devices.
14. As a user opening an old Project file, I want it to load without changes, so that provenance support does not damage existing work.
15. As a user saving provenance, I want older applications to reject the file, so that they cannot silently erase unknown data.
16. As a user exporting conversation Markdown, I want readable provenance included, so that the export retains the evidence shown in ThoughtTree.
17. As a user continuing a conversation, I want provenance excluded from prompts, so that metadata does not alter model context.
18. As a user viewing a large Graph, I want Graph cards to stay quiet, so that provenance does not obscure conversation structure.
19. As an importer developer, I want provider-neutral provenance types, so that Codex data does not leak Provider-specific shapes into the Graph.
20. As a live-capture developer, I want the same provenance model, so that imported and live Turns use one presentation and persistence path.

## Implementation Decisions

- Turn provenance is optional and belongs only to an assistant GraphNode.
- Turn provenance is best-effort evidence, not an audit trail.
- Provenance completeness is `complete`, `partial`, or `unknown`.
- `complete` means that the adapter observed the full Turn and retained every supported item.
- `partial` means that a known loss occurred. `unknown` means that the source cannot determine whether loss occurred.
- A GraphNode without Turn provenance makes no completeness claim.
- The assistant GraphNode content remains the exact final answer.
- Conversation-path construction ignores Turn provenance.
- Turn references form the canonical persisted source for provenance views.
- Reference order follows first appearance. Relations are additive and record observed evidence only.
- URL relations are `consulted` and `cited`.
- File relations are `mentioned`, `read`, `created`, and `modified`.
- URL text remains exact. Deduplication uses exact string equality.
- Only HTTP and HTTPS references are clickable. Project loading never fetches or validates a URL.
- Vault files use normalized Vault-relative paths.
- External file references retain only a non-clickable display name.
- Turn activity is one persisted ordered sequence. Array order is authoritative, and timestamps are optional metadata.
- Turn activity contains Assistant commentary, Tool activity, and Unknown activity.
- Assistant commentary contains verbatim user-visible progress text. It excludes hidden reasoning and chain-of-thought.
- One Tool activity represents one logical invocation. Provider lifecycle updates refine the same item.
- Tool state is `pending`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `failed`, or `incomplete`.
- A nonterminal Tool activity becomes `incomplete` when its Turn closes. A terminal state never regresses.
- Tool kind is `read`, `edit`, `delete`, `move`, `search`, `execute`, `fetch`, `delegate`, or `other`.
- Tool activity stores a local stable ID, title, kind, state, optional timestamps, and related Turn-reference IDs.
- Tool titles are untrusted plain text with a 200-character limit. The UI identifies truncated titles.
- This version does not store raw tool input, raw tool output, command text, or generated tool summaries.
- Unknown activity stores only a safe type name, display label, and position in Turn activity.
- Unknown activity does not retain its raw payload. Its presence makes provenance partial.
- Project-file version 4 introduces Turn provenance and explicit migration from every currently supported legacy format.
- Older applications reject version 4 instead of loading and later erasing unknown provenance.
- Markdown subgraph export includes a human-readable provenance section for each included assistant GraphNode.
- The SidePanel keeps the exact answer as its primary content.
- One collapsed `Provenance` disclosure appears below the answer.
- The disclosure label shows source, file, and activity counts.
- References appear before the chronological activity list.
- Commentary and Tool-activity details start collapsed.
- Partial and unknown provenance show a warning.
- Graph cards do not show provenance in this version.
- Optional Provider session and Turn identifiers are outside this version.
- If origin identifiers are added later, they are descriptive metadata. They do not establish identity or re-import behavior.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests assert observable behavior. They do not assert internal component structure or normalization helper calls.
- Use one sanitized version-4 fixture across the highest practical seams.
- The fixture contains an exact answer, one URL, one Vault file, commentary, Tool activity, and Unknown activity.
- The fixture also covers additive relations, activity order, incomplete provenance, and a truncated title.
- At the Project behavior seam, load the fixture through the Graph store and save it again.
- The Project test compares the observable Graph data and exact assistant content after the round trip.
- The Project seam also loads every currently supported legacy format and preserves its existing Graph data.
- At the conversation seam, build a Conversation path from the fixture and assert that provenance is absent.
- At the export seam, export the same lineage to Markdown and assert that its readable provenance is present.
- At the SidePanel seam, render the fixture's assistant GraphNode and interact with the provenance disclosure.
- SidePanel tests cover counts, reference relations, ordering, warnings, collapsed details, truncation, and safe link behavior.
- Pure Graph-model tests cover serialization and the discriminated provenance shapes.
- Existing Graph serialization tests provide prior art for round-trip and legacy migration behavior.
- Existing Graph-model tests provide prior art for Conversation-path assertions.
- Existing Graph-store tests provide prior art for Project persistence and Markdown subgraph export.
- Existing SidePanel component tests provide prior art for user-visible interaction assertions.
- The repository test suite and production build must pass.

## Out of Scope

- Historical session discovery, Turn selection, and Codex import transport.
- Origin identity, duplicate detection, merge behavior, and idempotent re-import.
- Live ACP event transport, accumulation, and association with a streaming GraphNode.
- Raw tool input, raw tool output, terminal logs, and replay of historical activity.
- Automated secret detection or redaction of arbitrary answer and commentary text.
- Graph-card badges or other provenance signals on the Graph.
- Clickable external file paths.
- A control that strips provenance from exports.
- A new structured Project-subgraph export format.
- Advanced recovery for malformed or conflicting Provider lifecycle streams.

## Further Notes

Imported provenance is untrusted historical data. Rendering must not execute tool input, open external paths, or broaden ThoughtTree permissions.

The historical-import epic and live-capture epic depend on this shared model. Both epics must normalize Provider data before it reaches Graph types.

The domain glossary defines Turn provenance, Turn reference, Turn activity, Tool activity, Unknown activity, and Provenance completeness.

ADR 0006 records the Project-file version 4 decision and its data-loss rationale.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] A version-4 Project file preserves exact assistant content and provider-neutral Turn provenance.
- [ ] Every currently supported legacy Project format loads without provenance or Graph-data loss.
- [ ] Conversation paths remain unchanged when an assistant GraphNode has provenance.
- [ ] Markdown subgraph exports include readable provenance for included assistant GraphNodes.
- [ ] The SidePanel shows safe references and ordered activity in a collapsed disclosure.
- [ ] Partial and unknown completeness states are visible to the user.
- [ ] Unknown activity remains inspectable without retaining its raw payload.
- [ ] Raw tool input, raw tool output, command text, and external absolute paths are not persisted.
- [ ] The shared sanitized fixture passes the Project, Conversation, export, and SidePanel behavioral tests.
- [ ] The complete repository test suite and production build pass.

title: Parked permissions end-to-end (park, reattach-first surfacing, resume)
description:
## What to build

Parked permissions end-to-end (PRD: docs/prd/mobile-push.md; CONTEXT.md: Parked permission): an agent permission request that fires while no client is attached pends indefinitely — no timeout, no auto-deny — pauses its Turn, and is the first thing a reattaching client sees.

Most machinery exists: core's `PermissionBroker` already parks requests and exposes `pending()`; the Turn registry tracks `TurnState::AwaitingPermission`. This issue wires it through the server protocol and the PWA UX:

- `ServerEventSink.permission_request` → broadcast `{ "type": "permission-request", "turnId": ..., ...PermissionRequestEvent }` to attached clients AND flip the Turn's state to `AwaitingPermission`.
- `AttachSnapshot.parkedPermissions` populated from `PermissionBroker::pending()` (scoped to the graph's active Turn).
- New endpoint: `POST /api/permissions/{requestId}` body `{ "optionId": "..." }` → `broker.respond` → 200 | 404 (unknown/already answered). `HttpTransport.respondToPermission` maps to it.
- Turn state returns to `Streaming` when the broker resolves the request.

PWA UX: on snapshot containing parked permissions, show the permission modal before anything else (PRD: "surfaced first on reattach"); while a permission is parked and the client is attached, the existing permission prompt UI is reused — same component as desktop, driven through the transport events. Answering resumes the stream live.

Desktop path must remain byte-identical (same broker; `TauriEventSink` + `respond_to_permission` command already delegate to it).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Trigger a tool call requiring permission from the PWA, then detach all clients: Turn parks in `AwaitingPermission` (observable via journal/log or a state field on snapshot), no timeout fires
- [ ] Reattach: permission modal appears before any other UI action; approving resumes the Turn to completion; denying completes the Turn with the denied outcome
- [ ] Answering an already-answered/unknown request → 404, surfaced gracefully (modal dismisses)
- [ ] Two attached clients: both see the permission request; first answer wins, second gets the 404 path
- [ ] Desktop permission flow unchanged
- [ ] Tests: broker pending()-to-snapshot wiring; respond endpoint happy/404 paths

title: WebDAV vault backend: If-Match ETag CAS (spike first)
description:
## What to build

The WebDAV vault backend for shape C production: reads/list from the read-only NAS mount, writes through Nextcloud WebDAV with `If-Match` ETag as the compare-and-swap transport (ADR 0004: docs/adr/0004-guarded-project-writes.md). PRD flags ETag semantics as a named risk — so this issue starts with a timeboxed spike.

Spike first (record findings as comments on this issue before implementing):

1. `GET` a file via Nextcloud WebDAV — confirm response carries a usable ETag.
2. `PUT` with stale `If-Match` → expect 412; with current ETag → expect success + new ETag.
3. ETag stability: does the ETag change only on content change (vs. on sync/metadata events)?
4. Fallback decision if `If-Match` is unreliable: GET-hash-compare-PUT with narrower race window (documented, not silent).

Implementation — second `VaultStorage` impl in `thoughttree-core` (or a small `thoughttree-vault-webdav` module inside core; implementer's call, but it must stay MIT and behind the existing trait):

```rust
pub struct WebDavVault {
    http: reqwest::Client,
    base_url: url::Url,            // e.g. https://nas/remote.php/dav/files/{user}/{vault-subpath}/
    credentials: WebDavCredentials, // Nextcloud app password; from env, never logged
    /// Optional read-only bind mount of the same vault subtree, used ONLY for list()
    /// (fast directory walks). Reads use GET so content + ETag arrive atomically.
    list_root: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
}
```

Semantics mapping (Revision = ETag here; callers can't tell — it's opaque):

- `read` → `GET` (content + ETag in one response; never read content from the mount and ETag from PROPFIND separately — that pairing races)
- `write` with `expected: Some(rev)` → `PUT` + `If-Match: <etag>`; 412 → `VaultError::Stale { current }` (fetch current ETag for the error)
- `write` with `expected: None` → plain `PUT`
- `list` → walk `list_root` if configured, else `PROPFIND Depth: infinity` (or per-dir Depth 1 walk if the server rejects infinity)

Server config: `TT_STORAGE=local|webdav`, `TT_WEBDAV_URL`, `TT_WEBDAV_USER`, `TT_WEBDAV_PASSWORD` (env only), optional `TT_LIST_ROOT`. Security: credentials never in logs or error strings; HTTPS enforced for non-localhost URLs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Spike findings (ETag behavior, 412 semantics, stability) recorded on the issue; fallback documented if needed
- [ ] `WebDavVault` implements `VaultStorage`; stale write surfaces as 409 `{ current }` through the server API, driving the same Reload/Overwrite UX
- [ ] Guarded write round-trip against a real Nextcloud instance verified (manual integration run acceptable; scriptable preferred); a write is immediately visible to other Nextcloud sync clients
- [ ] `list()` works via mount path and via PROPFIND fallback
- [ ] Credentials sourced from env, absent from logs/errors
- [ ] Unit tests with a mocked WebDAV server for read/write/stale/list

- Guarded writes (VaultStorage trait)
- GATE: mobile-usage validation evidence

## What to build

The `thoughttree-server` crate (AGPL-3.0 from first commit — ADR 0005) plus the frontend `HttpTransport`, delivering the first browser-served slice: browse the Vault, open a graph, edit, guarded-save — the full project lifecycle over HTTP, no chat yet (PRD: docs/prd/mobile-push.md, M4 start + M5 start).

Server: new workspace member `crates/thoughttree-server` (axum + tokio), consuming `thoughttree-core`'s `VaultStorage` (LocalFsVault for now; WebDAV backend is a separate issue — keep the storage choice behind config).

HTTP API v1 (JSON; single stale-write convention = 409):

```
GET  /api/health                → 200 { "status": "ok", "version": "..." }
GET  /api/projects              → 200 [ { "relativePath": "...", "modifiedEpochMs": ... } ]
GET  /api/projects/{*path}      → 200 { "content": "...", "revision": "..." } | 404
PUT  /api/projects/{*path}
     body: { "content": "...", "baseRevision": "..." | null }
     → 200 { "revision": "..." } | 409 { "current": "..." } | 400
POST /api/graphs/{*path}/prompt → 501 (stub until the Turns issue)
Static fallback: serve the built PWA (vite dist/), SPA fallback to index.html
```

Config via env (document in crate README): `TT_VAULT_ROOT` (required), `TT_BIND` (default `0.0.0.0:7420`), `TT_DATA_DIR` (for later turn journal). Auth: none — tailnet membership is the v1 perimeter (PRD assumption); bind is expected to sit behind Tailscale in deployment. Path handling must reuse core's vault path validation (no traversal).

Frontend: `HttpTransport` implements `BackendTransport` for the project surface (`loadProject`/`saveProject`/`listProjects` → the API above; `sendPrompt` rejects with a clear "not yet available" until the Turns issue; `capabilities.nativeDialogs = false`). Transport selection at boot: Tauri runtime detected → `TauriTransport`, else `HttpTransport` against same-origin `/api`. Project picker UI for the no-native-dialogs case: list from `listProjects()`, open on tap — this replaces the desktop open-dialog flow in the PWA. PWA manifest (standalone display, icons) so iPad can install it.

Stale-save UX (Reload/Overwrite dialog from the guarded-writes issue) must work identically through `HttpTransport` — the 409 body maps to `StaleRevisionError`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `crates/thoughttree-server` with AGPL-3.0 LICENSE file; workspace still builds; core stays MIT
- [ ] API endpoints behave as specified incl. 409-with-current-revision on stale writes and 404 on missing project; path traversal rejected
- [ ] Server serves the built frontend; SPA fallback works
- [ ] In a desktop browser and iPad Safari (LAN): list vault, open a graph, edit a node, save; concurrent edit → 409 → Reload/Overwrite dialog works
- [ ] PWA installable on iPad (manifest + icons)
- [ ] Rust integration tests for the projects API against a temp vault (axum + LocalFsVault)

## Blocked by

- Frontend transport seam (BackendTransport)
- Cargo workspace split (thoughttree-core)

title: Cargo workspace split: crates/thoughttree-core + Tauri app crate
description:
## What to build

Split the Rust side into a cargo workspace so one core crate serves every deployment shape (PRD: docs/prd/mobile-push.md, M2; CONTEXT.md: Deployment shape):

- `crates/thoughttree-core` — MIT (own LICENSE file). Contains the Tauri-free backend: `types`, `events` (SessionEventSink + event structs), `permissions` (PermissionBroker), `acp/{clients,process,sessions}`, `runtime` (LocalSet helper). Zero `tauri` dependencies — this is the crate a future axum server and the existing desktop shell both consume.
- The Tauri app crate — keeps `main.rs`/`lib.rs`, `commands/*`, `config.rs` (tauri_plugin_store stays here; core receives plain values, which is already true after the de-Tauri prefactor), `TauriEventSink`, `tauri.conf.json`, build script, bundling.

Layout constraint, not prescription: core must live outside the Tauri app crate under `crates/`; whether the app crate stays at `src-tauri/` (Tauri tooling default) or moves to `crates/thoughttree-tauri` is the implementer's call — pick whatever keeps `bun run tauri dev` and `bun run tauri:build` working with minimal config (`tauri.conf.json` build paths, sidecar bundling unchanged).

License boundary per ADR 0005 (docs/adr/0005): core is MIT; the workspace layout must make the (future) AGPL server crate boundary obvious — put a LICENSE file in each crate now.

Update CI/dev commands from CLAUDE.md (`cargo fmt/clippy/test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml`) to workspace form, and update CLAUDE.md itself.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Cargo workspace with `crates/thoughttree-core` + Tauri app crate; `cargo test --workspace` passes
- [ ] `thoughttree-core` builds standalone and `cargo tree -p thoughttree-core` shows no `tauri` (enforced in CI or a test/script)
- [ ] `thoughttree-core` has an MIT LICENSE file
- [ ] `bun run tauri dev` and `bun run tauri:build` work; app identifier/bundle unchanged; zero user-visible change
- [ ] CLAUDE.md build commands updated to workspace paths

## Blocked by

- Backend de-Tauri prefactor (SessionEventSink + PermissionBroker)

title: GATE: mobile-usage validation evidence (remote-desktop stopgap)
description:
## What to build

Validation gate from the PRD (docs/prd/mobile-push.md, GATE after M3): before any server-side work starts, gather real evidence that mobile ThoughtTree usage is real — via the zero-code stopgap, remote desktop over Tailscale (Screens/Moonlight to the laptop running desktop ThoughtTree).

Not a code issue. Steps:

1. Set up remote desktop access from iPad to the Mac running ThoughtTree over Tailscale.
2. Use it for natural (not forced) ThoughtTree sessions for at least several days.
3. Record: number of real sessions, contexts (couch, travel, away-from-desk), what worked, what hurt (canvas interaction, text input, latency), and whether the pull to reach for it was real.
4. Decide go/no-go for the server milestones and record the decision + evidence summary in the PRD (Status line + short evidence note).

If usage is not real: stop the mobile push here — M1–M3 (GraphModel package, core extraction, guarded writes) already paid for themselves (PRD rationale).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Stopgap ran for a real usage period (not a one-off demo)
- [ ] Evidence summary recorded in docs/prd/mobile-push.md
- [ ] Go/no-go decision recorded; if go, server issues unblocked (this milestone closed)

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately (independent of code issues).

title: Extract graph-model TS package (packages/graph-model)
description:
## What to build

Extract the pure graph domain layer out of `src/lib/graph/` into a standalone workspace package `packages/graph-model` (npm name `@thoughttree/graph-model`), consumed by the app exactly as before. This is the prefactor that lets the canvas PWA, a future thread view, and a future Obsidian plugin share one implementation of graph semantics (PRD: docs/prd/mobile-push.md, M1).

Scope decision — purity boundary: the package contains only the ReactFlow-free modules: `types`, `model` (GraphModel), `mutations` (GraphMutations), `serialize` (GraphSerialize, GRAPH_JSON_VERSION). The ReactFlow projection (`projection.ts`, `graphToFlowNodes`/`graphToFlowEdges`, `FlowNode` types) stays in the app — it is presentation (see CONTEXT.md "ReactFlow projection") and must not drag `@xyflow/react` into the package's dependency tree.

Public API of the package = the current ReactFlow-free exports:

```ts
// packages/graph-model — public surface
export { GraphModel } from './model'
export { GraphMutations } from './mutations'
export { GraphSerialize, GRAPH_JSON_VERSION } from './serialize'
export type { Graph, GraphEdge, GraphJSON, GraphNode, NodeId, Position } from './types'
```

Set up bun workspaces in the root `package.json` (`"workspaces": ["packages/*"]`). Move the module tests (`model.test.ts`, `mutations.test.ts`, `serialize.test.ts`) into the package. App code and `projection.ts` import from `@thoughttree/graph-model`. Domain vocabulary: CONTEXT.md (Graph, GraphNode, GraphModel, Conversation path).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `packages/graph-model` exists as a bun workspace package; app imports `@thoughttree/graph-model`, no imports of the old `src/lib/graph` model/mutations/serialize paths remain
- [ ] Package has zero runtime dependencies; `@xyflow/react` does not appear anywhere in the package (deps or imports)
- [ ] `projection.ts` remains in the app and imports domain types from the package
- [ ] `bun test:run` passes; package tests run from the package
- [ ] `bun run build` (typecheck + vite) passes; app behavior unchanged

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately.
