title: SidePanel citation test must cover out-of-order indices and an uncited reference
description:
## Deferred review finding from Issue Run thoughttree-4hq.4

### Finding `agent-208732b7a54a407d` (low, src/components/SidePanel/SidePanel.test.tsx:319)

The new test claims to verify ordered cited/consulted references, but its references are already in index order and both are cited by the content. It therefore would not catch regressions that remove sorting or incorrectly label uncited references. Reverse the fixture reference order and add an indexed reference whose marker is absent, then assert it sorts correctly and displays “Consulted”.

**Evidence:** The added fixture at lines 319–336 supplies indexes 1 then 2, while the content at line 315 cites both 【1】 and 【2】. The targeted test command passed all 21 tests, confirming no existing assertion covers the missing cases.

**Failure scenario:** A future change breaks index sorting or labels every indexed source “Cited” -> this test still passes, allowing incorrect SidePanel provenance labels/order to merge.

title: Kagi parser: accurate size-limit error message and uncited fetched-page test case
description:
## Deferred low-severity review findings from Issue Run thoughttree-4hq.2

### Finding `agent-81137f8eb7243943` (low, packages/graph-model/src/kagi.ts:16)

The `input_too_large` message always names `KAGI_EXPORT_MAX_BYTES`, even when the public `maxBytes` argument uses a different limit. Callers using a stricter cap therefore receive a typed error with a false user-facing limit. Pass the effective limit into `KagiExportError` (and preferably expose it as `limitBytes`) or remove the configurable argument.

**Evidence:** A temporary Vitest probe called `parseKagiExport('{"version":1}', 1)` and observed `{"code":"input_too_large","message":"Kagi export exceeds the 16777216-byte input limit (13 bytes)","inputBytes":13}`.

**Failure scenario:** A transport configured with a 1-byte or otherwise custom import limit rejects a file correctly but displays that the 16,777,216-byte limit was exceeded, misleading the user and diagnostics about the active policy.

### Finding `agent-3b610577f2311716` (low, packages/graph-model/src/kagi.test.ts:45)

The required independence case is not covered: the fixture tests a cited fetched-page reference (`is_search_result: false`) and a consulted search result (`is_search_result: true`), but never an uncited fetched page. Add an uncited `is_search_result: false` reference and assert `relations: ['consulted']` so relation classification cannot accidentally become coupled to source kind.

**Evidence:** The expected references at lines 25-53 assert index 1 as false/cited, index 2 as true/cited, and index 3 as true/consulted; no false/consulted case exists. The focused suite still reports 7 passing tests, confirming the specified combination is currently untested.

**Failure scenario:** A future refactor that marks all fetched pages as cited regardless of inline markers could pass the current suite because no uncited fetched-page case asserts the required consulted relation.

title: Reset SidePanel Provenance disclosure open state when the previewed node changes
description:
## Deferred review finding from Issue Run thoughttree-81u.3

### Finding `agent-2d1f724666aea5e8` (medium, src/components/SidePanel/index.tsx:217)

Key or explicitly reset the uncontrolled Provenance disclosure when `previewNodeId` changes. React currently reuses the same `<details>` element between assistant nodes, preserving its browser-mutated `open` attribute; nested commentary/tool disclosures can likewise retain their expanded state. Rendering `<Provenance key={previewNodeId} ... />` or controlling/resetting disclosure state would restore collapsed-by-default behavior. Add a test that expands provenance/activity on one assistant node and then selects another provenance-bearing node.

**Evidence:** Temporary exact-commit regression test: `NODE_OPTIONS=--require=/tmp/thoughttree-localhost-dns.cjs npm test -- --run src/components/SidePanel/ProvenanceSwitch.review.test.tsx` exited 1. After opening node A's disclosure and rerendering with node B selected, Testing Library reported `Expected the element not to have attribute: open; Received: open=""`.

**Failure scenario:** Trigger: expand Provenance or a nested activity disclosure for assistant node A, then select assistant node B that also has provenance. Because the unkeyed uncontrolled `<details>` DOM is reused, node B opens with provenance or activity details already expanded instead of presenting the required collapsed disclosure.

title: Resolve Kagi citation markers to provenance references in the SidePanel
description:
## Outcome

Inline `【n】` citation markers in an imported Kagi answer resolve to the matching provenance reference in the SidePanel, so the user can see which source backs which claim.

## Behavior

- Markdown content is not modified. Markers remain literal text in the GraphNode.
- The SidePanel provenance section (thoughttree-81u.3) lists references ordered by `index`, marks each as cited or consulted, and shows source kind (search hit vs fetched page) from `is_search_result`.
- Markers whose index has no matching reference are left as plain text and the provenance section notes the gap.
- Optional stretch: render `【n】` as a superscript link to the reference entry within the SidePanel only, never in exports.

## Success Criteria

[ ] Fixture answer shows its `【1】` marker unchanged in content.
[ ] Provenance section lists cited and consulted references with correct labels.
[ ] A marker with no matching reference does not crash rendering.
[ ] Markdown subgraph export (thoughttree-81u.2) includes the references without altering the answer text.
